app.name: Hejmo
firststeps.title: First steps
firststeps.lead: This is how you fill Hejmo with your family life. The order helps; every step can be skipped.
firststeps.skipped.text: Skipped. You can catch up any time.
firststeps.hide.hint: You will find them under Settings.
firststeps.settled: All done. Hejmo now knows your family.
firststeps.close.hint: After that the start page shows your day. You will find the steps under Settings.
firststeps.family.title: Add the family
firststeps.family.text: Add your partner and the children, up to 8 people. Each person gets a colour and a marker. This way even children who cannot read yet find themselves on the display.
firststeps.parents.title: Invite the second parent
firststeps.parents.text: Add the second parent. Then you connect your personal devices, so you always have Hejmo with you.
firststeps.calendars.title: Connect a calendar
firststeps.calendars.text: Connect iCloud, Google or another calendar. For each calendar you choose who it is for: the whole family or single people. Without a calendar of your own you use the box's calendar.
firststeps.tasks.title: Tasks or routine
firststeps.tasks.text: Add tasks that repeat, for example in the morning: brush teeth, get dressed, pack the school bag. Children earn stars for ticking them off.
firststeps.meals.title: Shopping list and meal plan
firststeps.meals.text: Plan the week's meals, and they show on the display. Put what you need on the shopping list.
firststeps.display.title: Hang the first display
firststeps.display.text: A tablet or E-Ink display on the wall shows your day, easy to see for everyone. Hejmo only asks you: "Where does it hang?"
flash.first_steps_hidden: First steps hidden. You will find them under Settings.
flash.first_steps_shown: First steps are back on the start page.
hub.first_steps.hint: Shows the steps that help you set up on the start page again.
setup.welcome.title: Welcome to Hejmo
setup.welcome.lead: You set up your box here. It takes about 15 minutes. You can stop in between: the box remembers how far you got.
setup.welcome.step.1: The box gets a certificate, so passwords and appointments are sent encrypted.
setup.welcome.step.2: Your town, your name, your password and a PIN for the display.
setup.welcome.step.3: An app on your device shows you a code when you sign in. This protects your account.
setup.welcome.step.4: After that the start page guides you: add the family, connect a calendar, hang the first display. Every step can be skipped.
setup.welcome.need.app: Your device with an authenticator app, for example [2FAS](https://2fas.com/), [Aegis](https://getaegis.app/) (Android only) or [Google Authenticator](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/1066447).
setup.welcome.need.desec: For the way with a free name: a free account at [deSEC](https://desec.io/signup). Step 1 shows you how.
setup.https.choice.title: How should people reach the box securely?
setup.https.choice.lead: Personal devices and computers talk to the box only in encrypted form. For that it needs a certificate. There are three ways, all three encrypt equally well. They differ in what you need and what goes outside.
setup.https.way.public: With a free name at deSEC
setup.https.way.own.means: The box issues its own certificate. It works only at your place, in the home network. For HTTPS nothing goes outside: no account, no name on the internet.
setup.https.way.own.cost: Every personal device and computer has to trust the box once. You install its certificate, about 2 minutes per device.
setup.https.way.public.means: The box gets a name like familie.dedyn.io. Every device trusts it at once, without installing anything.
setup.https.way.public.cost: The name is public on the internet. It only points to your box at home; it still cannot be reached from outside.
setup.https.way.domain.means: The box gets a name under your domain, for example box.familie-mueller.de. Every device trusts it at once, without installing anything.
setup.https.way.domain.need: a domain at Cloudflare, deSEC, Hetzner or INWX and access to its DNS settings.
setup.https.way.domain.cost: The name is public on the internet. It only points to your box at home; it still cannot be reached from outside.
setup.https.error.way: Choose one of the three ways. Then you can continue.
setup.https.own.means.1: The box works only when the device is in the home network: at home, or away from home through a VPN such as WireGuard.
setup.https.own.means.2: Every personal device and computer trusts the box once. The next page shows how, step by step, about 2 minutes per device. New devices later the same way.
setup.https.own.means.3: For HTTPS nothing goes outside: no account, no name on the internet, no certificate service.
setup.https.domain.title: Set up your own domain
setup.https.domain.lead: The box gets a name under your domain, for example ((box.familie-mueller.de)), and then gets the certificate by itself.
setup.https.domain.other: Is your domain at another provider? Then use the free name at deSEC or the box's own certificate:
setup.https.domain.pickfirst: Choose the provider above. The steps you need there then appear here.
setup.https.domain.cloudflare.sub: With an API token that may only change your domain.
setup.https.domain.desec.sub: With an access token from deSEC.
setup.https.domain.hetzner.sub: With an API token from the Hetzner Console.
setup.https.domain.inwx.sub: With user name and password; with two-factor sign-in, also its secret key.
setup.https.domain.cloudflare.heading: Domain at Cloudflare
setup.https.domain.desec.heading: Domain at deSEC
setup.https.domain.desec.token.title: Create an access token
setup.https.domain.desec.token.text: At deSEC, open [Token Management](https://desec.io/tokens), create a new token and paste it here. The box stores it encrypted.
setup.https.domain.hetzner.heading: Domain at Hetzner
setup.https.domain.inwx.heading: Domain at INWX
setup.https.domain.why.cloudflare.title: Why only for one domain?
setup.https.domain.why.cloudflare.text: A token that may only change the DNS records of this one domain leaves your other domains and settings at Cloudflare alone. The box stores it encrypted.
setup.https.domain.why.hetzner.title: Why a project of its own?
setup.https.domain.why.hetzner.text: A Hetzner token may do everything in the project, including servers in it. If your domain sits in a project just for DNS, the box cannot change anything else there. The box stores the token encrypted.
setup.https.domain.why.inwx.title: Why user name and password?
setup.https.domain.why.inwx.text: INWX offers no access that may only change DNS records. So the box signs in with your access. It only changes the box's name and, briefly, a check record for the certificate, stores everything encrypted and needs it regularly to renew the certificate.
setup.https.domain.name.title: Choose a name for the box
setup.https.domain.name.text: Choose a name under your domain, which is at {provider}. The box creates it by itself.
setup.https.domain.name.hint: A name under your domain. The box only points this one record to its address at home; all other records of the domain stay as they are.
setup.https.domain.cloudflare.token.text: At Cloudflare, under [API Tokens](https://dash.cloudflare.com/profile/api-tokens), create a token from the template **Edit zone DNS**. Under zone resources choose only your domain and add the permission **Zone › Zone › Read**.
setup.https.domain.cloudflare.zone_token: Only needed if the first token may not read zones. This second token only needs **Zone › Zone › Read**.
setup.https.domain.hetzner.token.title: Create an API token
setup.https.domain.hetzner.token.text: In the [Hetzner Console](https://console.hetzner.com/) open the project your domain is in, then **Security › API tokens**. Create a token with **Read & Write** and paste it here.
setup.https.domain.inwx.login.title: Enter your INWX access
setup.https.domain.inwx.login.text: The user name and password you sign in to INWX with.
setup.https.domain.inwx.twofa.title: Two-factor sign-in
setup.https.domain.inwx.twofa: Does INWX ask for a code from an app?
setup.https.domain.inwx.twofa.on: On: The box needs the secret key.
setup.https.domain.inwx.twofa.off: Off: User name and password are enough.
setup.https.domain.inwx.twofa.why: At every sign-in INWX asks for a 6-digit code from your app. For the box to renew the certificate without you, it needs the **secret key** the app makes these codes from.
setup.https.domain.inwx.twofa.where: You only see it when you set up two-factor sign-in at [INWX](https://www.inwx.de/de/customer/security): as text under the QR code. If you set it up again for this, scan the QR code with your app again too.
setup.https.domain.inwx.secret.hint: 16 to 32 letters and digits, for example JBSW Y3DP EHPK 3PXP. Not the 6-digit code.
setup.https.invalidhost: This address cannot be used for HTTPS. Open the box by its IP address or a name such as hejmo.local.
setup.https.own.title: Set up for the home network only
setup.https.own.lead: The box issues its own certificate. It is valid only for the box and cannot vouch for any other website.
setup.https.own.hint: Open the box under one of these addresses. Under another name, the browser warns.
setup.https.public.title: Set up a public name
setup.https.public.lead: You get a name and an access token from deSEC. The box then gets the certificate itself.
setup.https.public.s1.title: Create an account at deSEC
setup.https.public.s1.text: deSEC is a non-profit association from Berlin. The account is free.
setup.https.public.s2.title: Create a name
setup.https.public.s2.text: At deSEC, open [Domains](https://desec.io/domains), create a name that ends in **.dedyn.io** and enter it here.
setup.https.public.s3.title: Create an access token
setup.https.public.s3.text: At deSEC, open [Token Management](https://desec.io/tokens), create a new token and paste it here. The box stores it encrypted.
setup.https.public.name: Name of the box
setup.https.public.lan_ip: Address of the box at home
setup.https.public.lan_ip.hint: Your devices reach the box in your home network under this address. Already filled in with the address you are using now.
setup.https.public.issuer.actalis.hint: From Italy (EU). Needs a free account; the box then asks for the key ID and HMAC key.
setup.https.public.email.hint: With an email address the box can fall back to ZeroSSL when Let's Encrypt cannot be reached.
setup.https.public.terms: With "Get certificate" you accept the terms of the chosen certificate authority.
setup.https.public.busy: The box is getting the certificate …
setup.https.public.busy.hint: This usually takes under a minute, at most 3 minutes. Keep this page open.
setup.https.public.failed: The box could not get the certificate. Most often the token is wrong, or the name does not belong to this deSEC account. Check both and try again.
setup.https.error.invalid: Please check your entries and try again.
setup.https.error.name: This name does not work. It needs at least one dot and only lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, for example box.familie-mueller.de.
setup.https.error.lan_ip: That is not an address in your home network. It looks like this, for example: 192.168.178.40.
setup.https.error.eab: Enter the key ID and HMAC key of your Actalis account.
setup.https.error.token_again: Please paste the token again. The box does not keep it after an error.
setup.https.public.failed.cloudflare: The box could not get the certificate. Most often the token may not change your domain, or it lacks Zone › Zone › Read. Check both at Cloudflare and try again.
setup.https.public.failed.hetzner: The box could not get the certificate. Most often the token is wrong, or it belongs to a project your domain is not in. Check both in the Hetzner Console and try again.
setup.https.public.failed.inwx: The box could not get the certificate. Most often INWX refused the sign-in: the password is wrong, or the secret key belongs to an older two-factor sign-in. Check both and try again.
setup.https.error.name_taken: {name} already points to the address {address}, probably your website. The box does not overwrite it. Choose a name of its own, for example {suggestion}.
setup.https.error.otp_secret: That is not a secret key but probably the 6-digit code. The key has 16 to 32 characters: letters A to Z and digits 2 to 7.
setup.https.error.otp_secret_missing: That is empty. Please paste the secret key that INWX showed when you switched on two-factor sign-in. It has 16 to 32 characters.
setup.https.error.password_again: Please enter the password again. The box does not keep it after an error.
setup.https.error.secret_again: Please paste the secret key again. The box does not keep it after an error.
setup.https.error.zone_token_again: Please paste the second token again. The box does not keep it after an error.
setup.https.check.title: Check the name
setup.https.check.lead: The certificate is here. Now your browser checks whether it reaches the box under its new name.
setup.https.check.fail: Your browser does not reach **{name}** yet.
setup.https.check.last: This page checks again every 5 seconds. Last try: {time}
setup.https.check.ok: Your browser reaches the box under **{name}**.
setup.https.check.ok.hint: From now on, open the box under this name. It works on every device in your home network.
setup.https.rebind.title: Most often the router blocks the name
setup.https.rebind.why: The name points to an address in your home. Many routers refuse that as protection (DNS rebind protection). Add the name as an exception. On a FRITZ!Box it works like this:
setup.https.rebind.s1.title: Open the home network settings
setup.https.rebind.s1.text: Open [fritz.box](http://fritz.box/) and there [[Home Network › Network › Network settings › Additional settings › Home network]].
setup.https.rebind.s2.title: Add the exception
setup.https.rebind.s2.text: Under [[DNS rebind protection]] add this name:
setup.https.rebind.s3.title: Apply and check
setup.https.rebind.s3.text: Click "Apply" in the FRITZ!Box. This page notices by itself.
setup.https.rebind.other: Another router? Look in its settings for "DNS rebind protection" or a list of allowed names.
setup.https.ownca.title: Cannot change the router?
setup.https.ownca.text: Then use the box's own certificate. The public name is forgotten. Afterwards you install the certificate once on every device.
setup.title: Your account
setup.lead: This is how you sign in to Hejmo. You add other parents and the children afterwards.
setup.step.home.hint: The town gives the weather and the sunrise and sunset, the state the public holidays.
setup.step.pin.hint: Parents need the PIN at the display, for example to delete a whole list. Children should not know it.
setup.field.name: Your name
setup.field.name.hint: This is how you appear on the display.
setup.field.username.hint: You sign in with it. Lower-case letters are easiest.
setup.error.region: Please choose a state or canton.
setup.error.name: Please enter your name and a username.
setup.error.password: The password is too short. It needs at least 10 characters.
setup.error.code: That code is wrong. Use the code that is in the app right now. If it is wrong again, check that your device's clock is right.
setup.totp.title: Set up the one-time code
setup.totp.lead: When you sign in you need, besides your password, a code from an app on your device. This way nobody gets into your box with just your password.
setup.totp.s1.title: Open an authenticator app
setup.totp.s1.text: Open the app you use to create codes.
setup.totp.s1.install.desktop: Don't have one? 2FAS is free: [for iPhone in the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/2fas-auth/id1217793794) or [for Android on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.twofasapp). [Aegis](https://getaegis.app/) or [Google Authenticator](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/1066447) work too.
setup.totp.s1.install.android: Don't have one? [Get 2FAS on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.twofasapp); it is free. [Aegis](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.beemdevelopment.aegis) works too.
setup.totp.s1.install.ios: Don't have one? [Get 2FAS in the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/2fas-auth/id1217793794); it is free. [Google Authenticator](https://apps.apple.com/app/google-authenticator/id388497605) works too.
setup.totp.scan.title: Scan the QR code
setup.totp.scan.text: In the app, tap "Add" or "+" and scan this code.
setup.totp.key: QR code does not work? Type the key
setup.totp.key.text: In the app, choose "Enter key" and type:
setup.totp.personal_device.title: Add Hejmo in the app
setup.totp.personal_device.text: Tap the button and choose your authenticator app.
setup.totp.other: The app is on another device?
setup.totp.other.text: Scan this QR code with the other device.
setup.totp.qr: QR code of the one-time code key. Scan it with the authenticator app.
setup.totp.s3.title: Enter the code
setup.totp.s3.text: The app now shows a 6-digit code for Hejmo. It changes every 30 seconds.
trust.title: Trust the box
trust.lead: For your device to trust the box, you install its certificate once. It is valid only for the box. This takes about 2 minutes.
trust.devices.label: Choose a device
trust.detected.unknown: Your device was not detected. Choose it.
trust.steps.title: {device}: 4 steps
trust.waiting: Your {device} does not trust the box yet.
trust.fail: Your {device} does not trust the box yet.
trust.fp.title: Compare the fingerprint (optional)
trust.fp.what: The fingerprint is like a serial number: every certificate has its own. If your device shows a **SHA-256** fingerprint while installing, it must look exactly like this. Compare at least the first and the last line.
trust.fp.mismatch: If it does not match, do not install the certificate. The box's log names the same fingerprint; comparing there is the stronger check.
trust.windows.mismatch: Windows shows only SHA-1, so there is nothing to compare while installing. Check the SHA-256 fingerprint above against the box log.
trust.skip.title: The check does not work?
trust.skip.text: Some browsers do not allow the check. If you did all the steps, you can continue anyway. If the browser then shows a warning, the certificate is still missing.
trust.later: You set up the family's other personal devices and computers later. When you connect a personal device or display, the box shows you the way.
trust.ios.1.title: Download the profile
trust.ios.1.text: Tap the button. If your device asks whether it may download the profile, tap "Allow".
trust.ios.1.after: Downloaded. Next you install the profile.
trust.ios.2.title: Install the profile
trust.ios.2.text: Open [[Settings]]. At the top it says [[Profile Downloaded]]. Tap it, then "Install", and enter your device's passcode.
trust.ios.3.title: Turn on trust
trust.ios.3.text: Open [[Settings › General › About › Certificate Trust Settings]] and turn on [[Hejmo box CA]].
trust.ios.3.fail: Is [[Hejmo box CA]] turned on in the certificate trust settings? It is a separate switch that only exists after installing.
trust.ios.4.title: Come back here
trust.ios.4.text: This page notices by itself when your device trusts the box.
trust.ios.fp: Where to find it: while installing, under "More Details".
trust.android.1.title: Download the certificate
trust.android.1.text: Tap the button. The file hejmo-ca.crt lands in your Downloads folder.
trust.android.1.after: Downloaded: hejmo-ca.crt in your Downloads folder.
trust.android.2.title: Install the certificate
trust.android.2.text: Open [[Settings › Security › More security settings › Install a certificate › CA certificate]] and choose hejmo-ca.crt.
trust.android.2.hint: The names differ a little by manufacturer. Search the settings for "CA certificate".
trust.android.3.title: Confirm the warning
trust.android.3.text: Android warns that someone could read along. The certificate is valid only for the box; tap "Install anyway".
trust.android.3.fail: Is the certificate installed as a "CA certificate"? As a "VPN and app user certificate" or "Wi-Fi certificate" it is not enough.
trust.android.4.title: Come back here
trust.android.4.text: Come back to this browser. This page notices by itself when your device trusts the box.
trust.android.after: Firefox uses its own certificates: [[Settings › Privacy & Security › View Certificates › Authorities › Import]], or it will not trust the box. Calendar apps such as DAVx5 ask once more when you first connect whether they should trust the certificate. Confirm it once.
trust.android.fp: Where to find it: Settings › Security › Trusted credentials › User › Hejmo box CA.
trust.mac.1.title: Download the certificate
trust.mac.1.text: Click the button. The file hejmo-ca.crt lands in your Downloads folder.
trust.mac.1.after: Downloaded: hejmo-ca.crt in your Downloads folder.
trust.mac.2.title: Put it in the keychain
trust.mac.2.text: Open [[Keychain Access]], choose the keychain [[login]] on the left and drag hejmo-ca.crt into it. Do not double-click the file.
trust.mac.3.title: Always trust
trust.mac.3.text: Double-click [[Hejmo box CA]], expand [[Trust]] and under "When using this certificate" choose [[Always Trust]]. Close the window and confirm with your Mac password.
trust.mac.3.fail: Does [[Hejmo box CA]] say [[Always Trust]] under "Trust"? After closing the window the Mac asks for your password.
trust.mac.4.title: Come back here
trust.mac.4.text: This page notices by itself when your Mac trusts the box.
trust.mac.after: Firefox uses its own certificates: [[Settings › Privacy & Security › View Certificates › Authorities › Import]].
trust.mac.fp: Where to find it: in Keychain Access at "Hejmo box CA" under "Fingerprints", SHA-256.
trust.windows.1.title: Download the certificate
trust.windows.1.text: Click the button. The file hejmo-ca.crt lands in your Downloads folder.
trust.windows.1.after: Downloaded: hejmo-ca.crt in your Downloads folder.
trust.windows.2.title: Install the certificate
trust.windows.2.text: Double-click hejmo-ca.crt and choose [[Install Certificate]] and [[Current User]]. Then choose [[Place all certificates in the following store]], [[Browse]] and [[Trusted Root Certification Authorities]].
trust.windows.3.title: Confirm the warning
trust.windows.3.text: Windows warns about a new root certification authority. The certificate is valid only for the box; confirm with "Yes".
trust.windows.3.fail: Is the certificate in "Trusted Root Certification Authorities"? Firefox uses its own certificates, see below.
trust.windows.4.title: Come back here
trust.windows.4.text: This page notices by itself when your computer trusts the box.
trust.windows.after: Firefox uses its own certificates: [[Settings › Privacy & Security › View Certificates › Authorities › Import]].
trust.windows.fp: While installing, Windows shows only a SHA-1 fingerprint. It is not the same as the box's SHA-256 fingerprint, so compare the one above with the box log.
trust.linux.1.title: Download the certificate
trust.linux.1.text: Click the button. The file hejmo-ca.crt lands in your Downloads folder.
trust.linux.1.after: Downloaded: hejmo-ca.crt in your Downloads folder.
trust.linux.2.title: Install the certificate
trust.linux.2.text: Open a terminal in the Downloads folder. On Debian and Ubuntu enter: [[sudo cp hejmo-ca.crt /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ && sudo update-ca-certificates]]
trust.linux.2.hint: Other distributions have their own folder for certificate authorities. Search for "add CA certificate" and your system's name.
trust.linux.3.title: Set up the browser
trust.linux.3.text: Chrome, Edge and Firefox use their own certificates. Import hejmo-ca.crt there under [[Settings › Privacy and security › Manage certificates › Authorities › Import]].
trust.linux.3.fail: Did you import hejmo-ca.crt in the browser as a certificate authority, with the tick for websites? The system alone is not enough for Chrome and Firefox.
trust.linux.4.title: Come back here
trust.linux.4.text: This page notices by itself when your computer trusts the box.
trust.linux.fp: Where to find it: in a terminal with [[openssl x509 -in hejmo-ca.crt -noout -fingerprint -sha256]].

connections.title: Connected services
connect.title: Connect a calendar
connect.lead: Hejmo fetches your events from where you already keep them. Nothing is deleted there.
connect.legend: Where do your events come from?

connect.icloud.sub: Calendars from iPhone, iPad and Mac.

connect.icloud.heading: Connect iCloud
connect.icloud.why: Hejmo never asks for your Apple password. You create an app-specific password just for Hejmo at Apple, and you can revoke it there at any time without changing your Apple password.
connect.icloud.step1.title: Sign in at Apple
connect.icloud.step1.text: Open your Apple Account page and sign in.
connect.icloud.step1.hint: Opens in a new tab. Keep this page open and come back here afterwards.
connect.icloud.step2.title: Open App-Specific Passwords
connect.icloud.notfound.text: The item only appears when two-factor authentication is on for your Apple Account. Turn it on on your iPhone: [[Settings]], then your name, then [[Sign-In and Security]]. Then reload the Apple page.
connect.icloud.help.label: support.apple.com/en-us/102654
connect.icloud.step3.title: Create a password for Hejmo
connect.icloud.step3.text: Create a new password and name it [[Hejmo]]. Apple asks for your Apple password once more: you enter it at Apple, not here. Then copy the password Apple shows you.
connect.icloud.step4.title: Enter it here
connect.icloud.step4.text: Your normal Apple password never goes into Hejmo.
connect.icloud.username: Email address of your Apple Account

connect.caldav.step2.title: Create an app password

connect.ics.heading: Subscribe to a calendar link
connect.ics.why.title: What does subscribing mean?

connect.ics.step1.text: On the website of the school, club or town it is often called [[Subscribe to calendar]], [[iCal]] or [[ICS]]. Copy the address of the link, not a downloaded file.
connect.ics.find.summary: Where do I find the link?

connect.ics.find.waste: **Waste collection:** in your town's waste calendar, often as [[iCal]] or [[Add to calendar]].

mcp.explain.title: What is MCP?
mcp.explain.what: AI assistants such as Claude or ChatGPT can do more than answer questions: they can also look things up in other programs and enter things. **MCP** (Model Context Protocol) is the common language for this. When you switch MCP on, your Hejmo box understands that language.
mcp.explain.say: You can then say to the assistant, for example:
mcp.explain.say1: “Add Mia's parents' evening on Tuesday at 7:30 pm.”
mcp.explain.say2: “Put milk and oats on the shopping list.”
mcp.explain.say3: “Plan five quick dinners for next week.”
mcp.explain.may1: Only what you choose for the token: events, lists, tasks (with routines and stars) and the meal plan, each read only or also changing.
mcp.explain.may2: Never: change settings, create tokens, manage people, displays or personal devices.
mcp.explain.know1: What the assistant reads, it sends to its provider so the AI can answer. Give it only the areas it needs.
mcp.explain.know2: A token belongs to the parent who creates it; the assistant acts as that person. Children get no MCP token.
mcp.explain.know3: The box speaks MCP only encrypted (HTTPS). It is usually reachable only on your home network; then the assistant has to run on a device on your home network. The guide shows how.

connect.outlook.name: Outlook
connect.outlook.heading: Connect Outlook
outlook.why.title: Why sign in at Microsoft?
connect.outlook.why: Hejmo never sees your Microsoft password. You sign in at Microsoft yourself and allow Hejmo there to read and change your calendars. You can withdraw that at Microsoft at any time.
connect.outlook.step1.title: Get a code
connect.outlook.step1.text: Hejmo gets a sign-in code for you from Microsoft. It is valid for 15 minutes.
connect.outlook.step2.title: Sign in at Microsoft
connect.outlook.step2.text: On this device or on another device: enter the code, sign in with your Microsoft account and choose **Accept**.
connect.outlook.step3.title: Choose calendars
connect.outlook.step3.text: This page notices by itself when you are done and shows you your Outlook calendars.
connect.outlook.work.summary: With a work or school account?
connect.outlook.work.text: Works too, with Microsoft 365 from a company, school or university. Some companies only allow apps like Hejmo once their IT has approved them. Then Hejmo tells you after signing in what you can send to your IT.
connect.outlook.appid: App ID of your own app registration
connect.outlook.appid.hint: Leave empty and Hejmo uses the Hejmo project's app registration. Only needed if you created your own at Microsoft. Microsoft calls the app ID "Application (client) ID".
connect.outlook.help.label: Guide: your own app registration
outlook.error.no_app: The Hejmo project has not set up an app registration for Outlook yet. Enter the app ID of your own app registration under "More options".
outlook.error.unknown_app: Microsoft does not know this app ID. Copy it at Microsoft from "Overview", field "Application (client) ID": 36 characters with four hyphens.
outlook.error.down: Microsoft is not answering right now, so there is no code yet. Try again in a few minutes.
outlook.signin.title: Sign in at Microsoft
outlook.signin.lead: To connect Outlook. This takes about two minutes.
outlook.signin.step1.title: Copy the code
outlook.signin.step1.text: You enter this code at Microsoft in a moment.
outlook.signin.step1.done: The code was entered at Microsoft.
outlook.signin.code.label: Code: %s
outlook.signin.step2.title: Open Microsoft and enter the code
outlook.signin.step2.hint: Opens in a new tab. Keep this page open. On a device, type the same address.
outlook.signin.step3.title: Sign in and choose "Accept"
outlook.signin.step3.text: Sign in with the Microsoft account whose calendars should go on the box. Microsoft asks whether Hejmo may read and change your calendars: choose **Accept**.
outlook.signin.step3.done: Signed in and accepted at Microsoft.
outlook.signin.step3.reconnect: Sign in with {account}. Microsoft asks whether Hejmo may read and change your calendars: choose **Accept**.
outlook.signin.step3.reconnect.hint: If another account is already signed in at Microsoft, choose "Use another account" there.
outlook.signin.step4.title: Back here
outlook.signin.waiting: Hejmo is waiting for you to sign in at Microsoft.
outlook.signin.waiting.sub: This page moves on by itself. Last asked: {time}
outlook.signin.ok.sub: Hejmo is looking for your calendars. This continues in a moment.
outlook.fail.expired.sub: A code is valid for 15 minutes; this one was valid until {time}. Get a new one and enter it at Microsoft right away.
outlook.fail.declined: Microsoft did not give Hejmo access.
outlook.fail.declined.sub: "Cancel" or "Do not accept" was chosen at Microsoft. Hejmo has saved nothing.
outlook.fail.declined.next: Get a new code and choose **Accept** at the end at Microsoft, otherwise the box cannot show your calendars.
outlook.fail.consent: Your company or school has to approve Hejmo first.
outlook.fail.consent.sub: Microsoft accepted the sign-in, but the permission for Hejmo is missing.
outlook.fail.consent.text: You signed in with a work or school account. Its IT only allows apps like Hejmo once an administrator approves them.
outlook.fail.consent.ask: **Ask your IT for an approval.** Send them these details:
outlook.fail.consent.scopes: Read and write calendars (Calendars.ReadWrite), stay signed in (offline_access), read profile (User.Read)
outlook.fail.consent.personal: **Or connect a personal Microsoft account** (outlook.com, hotmail.com, live.com).
outlook.fail.consent.hint: Once your IT has approved Hejmo, get a new code.
outlook.fail.wrong: That was a different Microsoft account.
outlook.fail.wrong.sub: You signed in with {other}. Reconnecting only works with {account}, otherwise the calendars would no longer belong together.
outlook.fail.wrong.more: Do you want to connect {other} as well? You can do that under [Connect a calendar](/connections/new?service=outlook).
outlook.fail.down: Microsoft is not answering right now.
outlook.fail.down.sub: There is no new code. Try again in a few minutes.
outlook.fail.other.sub: Hejmo has saved nothing. Get a new code and try again.
outlook.reconnect.title: Reconnect Outlook
outlook.reconnect.lead: Sign in with {account}. Names, colours and who the calendars are for stay as they are.
outlook.reconnect.one: The Microsoft sign-in for {account} has expired. Since {since} no new events from this account reach the box; the existing ones stay visible.
outlook.reconnect.many: The sign-in has expired for {count} Microsoft accounts. No new events from them reach the box until someone signs in again; the existing ones stay visible.
outlook.reconnect.who: Anyone who knows the password of this Microsoft account can sign in again.
outlook.reconnect.label: Reconnect {account}
outlook.card.hint: Only in Hejmo. In Outlook it is still called {name}.
outlook.acc.rw: **Read and change:** What you enter on the box also appears in Outlook.
outlook.acc.shared: **Read only:** {who} shared it with you. It can only be changed in Outlook.
outlook.acc.box_ro: **Read only:** You set it to "Read only" on the box. It can only be changed in Outlook.

setup.offline.title: Should the box stay fully offline?
setup.offline.lead: You chose “Only in the home network”. The box can also manage entirely without the internet. Calendar, tasks, lists, meals, displays and personal devices in the home network work either way.
setup.offline.yes.means: The box connects to nothing outside your home network. In Settings you can see at any time that nothing went out.
setup.offline.yes.cost: no weather on the displays, no calendars from iCloud, Google or other servers on the internet. You bring updates to the box yourself, with a USB stick or upload; a guide shows how.
setup.offline.no: No, only what is needed may go out
setup.offline.no.means: The box fetches the weather, looks for updates every night and syncs the calendars you connect. Nothing else.
setup.offline.no.cost: These services see the internet address of your connection. You can switch off each connection separately later.
setup.offline.hint: You can change this at any time under Settings › Connections to the outside.
setup.offline.error: Choose one of the two answers.
hub.outside.hint: What the box fetches from the internet, such as weather, updates and calendars, and what it tried.
outside.lead: What the box connects to outside your home network. With offline mode, nothing goes outside any more.
outside.main.on: The box connects to nothing outside your home network. Calendar, tasks, lists, meals, displays and personal devices in the home network keep working.
outside.main.off: The box may go outside, but only for the connections that are on below.
outside.proof: No connection to the outside since {when}.
outside.single.hint.on: As long as offline mode is on, all are off and locked.
outside.single.hint.off: Every connection that is on may go outside. Only parents can change them.
outside.row.locked: Off, locked: offline mode is on
outside.weather.for: The weather of your home on the displays.
outside.weather.for_home: The weather for {home} on the displays.
outside.update.for: Looks for a new Hejmo version every night between 03:30 and 03:45. What happens then is set under Household › Automatic updates.

outside.images.for: Only when you give an article a picture from the web. The box downloads it once.

outside.updates.how: How to bring an update to the box:
outside.updates.days: Remind after this many days without an update

outside.refused.hint: Here a part of the box wanted to go outside and was stopped. None of it left the house. Newest first.
outside.refused.empty: No refused attempts yet. No part of the box has tried to go outside.
outside.scope: What offline mode does not cover
outside.scope.host.text: Offline mode applies to Hejmo itself. The operating system of the device the box runs on (Raspberry Pi OS, say) can still fetch the time from the internet (NTP) and load its own updates. Hejmo does not switch that off.
outside.scope.time.text: The device can also take the time from your router, such as the FRITZ!Box.
outside.scope.mcp.text: An AI assistant in the home network can keep using the box. What it reads can leave the house through it, because Claude or ChatGPT send it to their provider.

flash.offline_off: Offline mode is off. The box may go outside again, for the connections that are on.

outside.on.failed: Nothing was changed. The box can still be reached at {name} and is not offline.

https.away.hint.router: Through a VPN a personal device often cannot find hejmo.local. Then open the box under {name}.
https.router.title: Name in the router
https.router.text: Your router knows the box under a name of its own, in the FRITZ!Box for example hejmo.fritz.box. If you enter it here, the certificate is valid for that name too. Then you open the box at home and through a VPN under this name, without a warning.
https.router.field.hint: In the FRITZ!Box it is under Home Network › Network, at the box's device. You can change it there too, for example to “hejmo”.
https.router.why.title: After this, every device has to trust the box again.
https.router.why.text: A new name needs a new certificate of the box. Every personal device, computer and display installs it once, about 2 minutes per device. Until then the browser warns there.
https.router.saved: “{name}” is entered. The certificate is now valid for that name too.
https.trust.title: Now every device has to trust the box again
https.trust.text: The box has a new certificate for this. Until a device trusts it, the browser warns there, on this device too at the next click. Start with this device, then every other personal device, computer and display, about 2 minutes per device.
https.trust.hint: The page opens even without trust: {url}. Open it on every other device.
connect.google.name: Google
connect.google.sub: Google Calendar, with a Gmail or Google account
google.heading: Connect Google
google.effort: Set up once, about 20 minutes, best on a large screen. Other Google accounts of the family then only need the sign-in.
google.why.title: Why your own app registration?
google.why.text: Google only lets programs reach calendars with an app registration. Hejmo has no server of its own that sees your data, so you create your own at Google, free of charge. Your events only travel between Google and your box; Hejmo never sees your Google password.
google.s1.title: Create a project
google.s1.text: Sign in with your Google account and create a new project. Name it [[Hejmo]] and choose [[Create]].
google.s1.hint: Opens in a new tab. Keep this page open. All further links open your project as long as [[Hejmo]] is selected at the top.
google.s2.title: Turn on two interfaces
google.s2.text: Open both pages and choose [[Enable]] on each. One brings the events, the other the list of your calendars.
google.s3.title: Set up Google Auth Platform
google.s3.text: Choose [[Get started]]. App name: for example [[Hejmo Maier]], so you recognise it when signing in. Under [[Audience]] choose [[External]]. As email addresses enter your own.
google.s4.title: Allow Hejmo's redirect page
google.s4.text: Under [[Branding]], at [[Authorized domains]], add this domain, then choose [[Save]]:
google.s4.label: Authorized domain
google.s4.hint: This page of the Hejmo project brings you back to your box after signing in. It only passes on the one-time sign-in code; without your box it is useless.
google.s5.title: Add access to calendars
google.s5.text: Under [[Data access]] choose [[Add or remove scopes]], add this scope manually and choose [[Save]]:
google.s5.label: Scope
google.s6.title: Publish the app
google.s6.text: Under [[Audience]] choose [[Publish app]] until it says [[In production]]. You do not need a review by Google.
google.s6.caution: If it still says [[Testing]], the sign-in ends after 7 days and the box gets no more events.
google.s7.title: Create a client
google.s7.text: Under [[Clients]] choose [[Create client]]. Application type: [[Web application]], name: [[Hejmo box]]. At [[Authorized redirect URIs]] enter both addresses, each with [[Add URI]], then choose [[Create]]:
google.s7.caution: Google then shows the client ID and the client secret. Google shows the secret only this once: copy it right away or download the JSON file.
google.s8.title: Enter it here
google.s8.text: Google calls the app registration an “OAuth client”. Enter both values from the client.
google.field.client_secret.hint: Usually starts with GOCSPX-. The box stores it encrypted and never shows it again.
google.field.client_secret.retype: Please enter the client secret again: the page does not keep it after an error.
google.submit: Save and sign in at Google
google.done: Then you sign in at Google and choose which calendars the box shows.
google.error.client_id: That is not the whole client ID. It ends with **.apps.googleusercontent.com**: copy it with the copy button next to the client ID at Google.
google.error.client_secret: Enter the client secret Google showed when you created the client.
google.error.client_rejected: Google did not accept this client secret. Copy it again from your client at Google. If Google no longer shows it, add a new secret there and enter it here.
google.reg.lead: Your app registration at Google is already set up. For another account, such as Papa's, you only need the sign-in: about two minutes.
google.replace.text_none: Only needed if you created a new client at Google.
google.replace.text_one_a: Only needed if you created a new client at Google. The new app registration applies to all Google connections of the box:
google.replace.text_one_b: has to sign in again afterwards.
google.replace.text_many: Only needed if you created a new client at Google. Applies to all Google connections of the box; each has to sign in again afterwards:
google.signin.title: Sign in at Google
google.signin.lead: For the connection with Google. It takes about two minutes. Google shows a warning on the way that is right in your case.
google.signin.lead_fallback: For the connection with Google, the fallback way. It takes about three minutes.
google.resignin.title: Sign in at Google again
google.resignin.lead: Sign in with {account}. Names, colours, who the calendars are for, and changes waiting on the box all stay.
google.steps.heading: Read the steps once before you start
google.s.account.title: Choose the account
google.s.account.text: Sign in at Google with the account whose calendars should go on the box.
google.s.account.right: Sign in with the right account
google.s.account.right.text: Choose {account} at Google. If another account is signed in there, choose [[Use another account]].
google.s.warn.title: The warning is right for you
google.s.warn.text: Google shows “Google hasn’t verified this app” because you created the app yourselves. Choose [[Advanced]], then [[Go to … (unsafe)]] with your app name.
google.s.allow.title: Allow access to the calendars
google.s.allow.hint: Google words the access very broadly, up to “permanently delete”. Hejmo only deletes events at Google that you delete on the box.
google.s.back.title: Back to the box
google.s.back.text: Google sends you back here through the page hejmo-home.github.io. Then you choose the calendars.
google.sk.warn.caption: Roughly what Google shows (simplified):
google.sk.warn.title: Google hasn’t verified this app
google.sk.warn.dim: The app is requesting access to sensitive info in your Google Account …
google.sk.allow.caption: Then Google asks for access (simplified):
google.sk.allow.title: Hejmo Maier wants additional access to your Google Account
google.sk.allow.box: See, edit, share, and permanently delete all the calendars you can access using Google Calendar
google.open.hint: Hejmo sends you to Google. The sign-in is valid for 15 minutes.
google.err.400.title: Error 400: redirect_uri_mismatch
google.err.400.text: One of the two redirect URIs is missing in the client or has a typo. Check them under [[Clients]]; they have to read exactly:
google.err.401.title: Error 401: invalid_client
google.err.401.text: The client ID is wrong. Enter it again:
google.err.403.title: Error 403: access_denied
google.err.403.text: The app is still on “Testing” at Google. Set it to “In production” under [[Audience]], then sign in again here.
google.noreturn.summary: Not getting back to the box?
google.noreturn.text: If hejmo-home.github.io stays on screen or shows an error, take the fallback: at the end you copy an address and paste it here.
google.forced.title: Only the fallback works here
google.forced.text.b: . Google only sends you back to addresses with https or to an address in the home network.
google.forced.hint: Through the address in the home network the normal way works too:
google.fallback.heading: Fallback: paste the address
google.fallback.s1.title: Open Google in a new tab
google.fallback.s1.hint: Keep this page open. The sign-in is valid for 15 minutes.
google.fallback.s2.title: Sign in, warning, access
google.fallback.s2.text: As on the normal way: choose the account, at “Google hasn’t verified this app” choose [[Advanced]] and [[Go to … (unsafe)]], tick the calendars, [[Continue]].
google.fallback.s3.title: “Cannot be reached” is right here
google.fallback.s3.text: Afterwards the browser says it cannot reach 127.0.0.1. The sign-in is in the address at the top: copy the whole address from the address bar.
google.sk.addr.caption: This is how it looks at the end (simplified):
google.sk.addr.tap: Copy the whole address at the top
google.fallback.s4.title: Paste the address here
google.paste.error.none: This address holds no sign-in. Copy it only when the browser says “cannot be reached”: it starts with http://127.0.0.1:8099/ and contains “code=”.
google.paste.error.old: This address belongs to an older sign-in. Open Google again with step 1, then copy the new address.
google.paste.error.cancelled: According to this address you cancelled at Google. Nothing was saved. Open Google again and choose “Continue” at the end.
google.problem.stale.title: This sign-in is no longer valid.
google.problem.stale.text: It is older than 15 minutes or was started in another browser. Nothing was saved.
google.problem.used.title: This sign-in was already used.
google.problem.used.text: That happens when the page is reloaded or you go back. If it just worked, you will find the connection under Calendar connections.
google.problem.code.title: Google did not confirm the sign-in.
google.problem.code.text: The sign-in code was already used or had expired. Nothing was saved.
google.problem.cancelled.title: You cancelled at Google.
google.problem.cancelled.text: Nothing was saved. At the end choose “Continue” at Google so that Hejmo may see your calendars.
google.problem.scope.title: Hejmo may not see your calendars yet.
google.problem.scope.text: You did not tick the calendars at Google. Sign in again and tick it before “Continue”. Nothing was saved.
google.problem.account.title: That was another Google account.
google.problem.account.text: You signed in as {wrong}. This connection belongs to {account}; nothing was changed.
google.problem.unreachable.title: Google cannot be reached right now.
google.problem.unreachable.text: The sign-in could not be completed. Nothing was saved. Try again in a moment.
connections.card.hint_google: Only in Hejmo. At Google it keeps the name {name}.
google.acc.rw.label: Read and change:
google.acc.rw.text: What you enter on the box also appears at Google.
google.acc.ro.label: Read only:
google.acc.ro.shared: Shared with you for viewing only. Changing is only possible at Google.
google.acc.ro.birthdays: Google fills it from your contacts.
google.access.title: What the box may change at Google
google.access.l1.b: Your own calendars and those that someone shares with you with “Make changes to events”:
google.access.l1.t: show, add and change events. What you enter on the box then also appears at Google.
google.access.l2.b: Calendars shared for viewing only, birthdays and holidays:
google.access.l3.t: Hejmo does not take over. Every calendar gets a colour in Hejmo; you change it under “More options”.
google.flag.signin: Sign-in expired: sign in at Google again
google.writeback.locked: Read only: it is shared with you for viewing only. Only whoever shares it can change that at Google.
google.login.label: Sign-in at Google
google.login.summary: Sign in again or change the app registration
google.login.text: The sign-in is valid. You only need to sign in again when Hejmo asks you to or you removed Hejmo's access in your Google account. Names, colours and who the calendars are for stay.
google.login.text_expired: Google no longer accepts the sign-in. Sign in again: names, colours and who the calendars are for stay.
google.remove.explain: The connection and these calendars disappear from the box and from the displays. Nothing is deleted at Google. Changes on the box that are not yet written back are lost.
google.remove.access: Afterwards you remove Hejmo's access in your Google account at [myaccount.google.com/connections]({url}). The app registration stays on the box so that other accounts can sign in without a new setup.
google.notice.text: Google no longer accepts the sign-in for {account}. Since {since} no new events from this account reach the box. The earlier ones stay visible; what you change on the box waits and is written back after you sign in.
google.notice.reasons: Common reasons: the Google password was changed, or Hejmo's access was removed in the Google account.
google.notice.seven: The sign-in lasted exactly 7 days. That almost always means your app is still on “Testing” at Google. Set it to “In production” under [[Audience]], then sign in again.
google.notice.who: Anyone who knows the password of this Google account can sign in again.
flash.google_signed_in: Signed in at Google. The calendars sync again now.
sync.fail.google_signin: Google no longer accepts the sign-in: sign in at Google again
sync.fail.google_client: Google does not accept the client ID or client secret: check the app registration
sync.fail.google_app: No app registration is entered for Google
sync.fail.google_token: Google refused the access token; it is renewed at the next sync
sync.fail.google_forbidden: Google refused this request (quota, rate limit or missing calendar permission); the box tries again at the next sync
layout.intro: What “{name}” shows and in which order. Each display has its own layout.
layout.state.saved: saved, this is what “{name}” shows now
layout.state.dirty: not saved yet, this is what it would look like
layout.words.fit.landscape: {n} columns fit side by side in landscape.
layout.words.fit.portrait: {n} columns fit side by side in portrait.
layout.words.none: Nobody chosen yet. Choose at least one person below.
layout.words.one: Only {person} chosen: “{name}” shows {person}’s personal view instead of columns, with tasks, routines and events of the next 7 days. Events for the whole family are included.
layout.error.people: Choose at least one person. For everyone tap “Whole family”.
layout.hint.whole: “Whole family” adds new people by itself, at the very end. Use the arrows to change the order: higher in the list means further left on the display.
layout.hint.some: If you choose single people, new ones only join when you tap them here. Use the arrows to change the order: higher in the list means further left on the display.
layout.off_tip: Tap to add them at the end.
layout.rotate.on: On: every day at 03:00 each person moves one column to the right, whoever is on the far right goes to the left. Tomorrow: {names}.
layout.rotate.off: Off: the order stays the same every day.
layout.family_always: Events for the whole family are always shown on every display, in the row above the columns.
layout.hint.blocks: The same goes for blocks: higher in the list means further left, in the columns further up.
layout.always.header: Always there: weekday, calendar week, date and, once there is a list, the “Lists” button.
layout.always.columns: Always there: marker and name at the top of each column.
layout.b.weather.on_nohome: On: sky and temperature at home
layout.b.events.off: Off: no events in the columns
layout.b.tomorrow_events.on: On: from 18:00 the first events of tomorrow, paler
layout.b.routines.on: On: each routine of today with its progress, for example “Morning: 2 of 4 done”
layout.b.routines.off: Off: no routines in the columns
layout.b.tasks.on: On: at the bottom of the column, for example “3 of 5 tasks done”
layout.b.meals.on: On: what is still to eat today
layout.b.tomorrow.on: On: tomorrow’s waste collection and the note for tomorrow
layout.b.list.on: On: the open entries of “{list}”. Tapping opens the whole list.
layout.b.list.on_none: On: the open entries of a list. Tapping opens the whole list.
layout.b.list.off: Off: no list at the bottom
layout.list.gone: The list “{name}” no longer exists. So “{display}” shows no list at the bottom. Choose another or switch the block off.
layout.list.none: You have no list yet. Create one under “Lists”, then you can show it here.
layout.hint.empty: A block without content stays off the display, for example “Meals today” when nothing is planned.
layout.why.columns: The personal view always shows tasks with routines and events. Your column settings stay saved and apply again as soon as you choose more than one person.
layout.why.footer: The personal view has no footer. These settings stay saved too.
layout.copy.summary: Copy the layout of another display
layout.copy.hint: Takes the people, order and blocks from there and saves this page. Name, brightness and quiet mode of “{name}” stay.
layout.copy.error: This display does not exist. Choose one from the list.
layout.list.more: {n} more. Tap here for the whole list.
